correctness.rationale: For a selected subset with a left vertices, b right vertices and d missing matching pairs, the induced graph has ab-d edges with d<=min(a,b,t). If a,b>=3, any selected 3-by-3 contains at least 9-3=6 edges on six vertices, hence a cycle; if (a,b) dominates (2,4) or (4,2), the 2-by-4 subgraph has at least 8-2=6 edges on six vertices, hence a cycle. The only forest cases left are subsets contained in one side; subsets with exactly one vertex of one side (a star possibly plus its unique nonadjacent matched vertex); (2,2) with precisely one missing matching pair yielding P4 or two missing pairs yielding 2K2; and (2,3)/(3,2) with exactly two missing matching pairs yielding P5. The one-small-side generating-function terms count unmatched/matched center choices and an isolate when the partner is selected; both directions double-count exactly (1,1) cross selections, whose adjacent/nonadjacent weights are subtracted. The one- and two-missing-edge 2-by-2 counts are t(p-1)(q-1)-t(t-1) and binom(t,2); the 2-by-3 count is binom(t,2)(p+q-4). This gives the asserted Phi for all p,q>=2 and 0<=t<=min(p,q). P4/P5 and maximum-induced-forest/feedback vertex consequences follow by reading coefficients, with crown special values (6,32,2n for n=3,4,n>=5). Independent new standard-library DFS enumeration for 163 parameter triples and 413040 vertex subsets confirmed all bivariate coefficients and both path counts, plus crown maxima n=3..9. A bounded check is corroboration only; the general theorem comes from exhaustive mathematical category proof.
residual_risks: Finite regression reaches p,q<=7 only; no exhaustive computation over all p,q.

evidence: Earlier non-CIS-pair theorem on the same G=K_{p,q}-M_t gives eta(G)=t((p-1)(q-1)-t+1). Its non-CIS pairs consist of a deleted matching pair plus an existing disjoint cross-part edge; those four vertices induce exactly one P4. Conversely every induced P4 determines that pair, proving eta(G)=N_{P4}(G) without relying on matching names.

Earlier geodesic-subpath counting theorem on the same family counts per missing edge ((p-1)(q-1)-t+1) length-3 shortest paths; summing t yields the same P4 count and shows that this submitted corollary was already implied.

Neither prior result conditions on arbitrary forest vertex subsets nor tracks components. A P5 is formed by selecting two missing disjoint edges and one additional third-side vertex, hence N_{P5}=binom(t,2)(p+q-4); this count and Phi are not fixed by the cited P4 identities.
Tittmann et al. 2011, Corollary 19, gives Q(K_{p,q};x,y) for the undeleted graph and counts cyclic subgraphs as well; it cannot be equated with Phi(K_{p,q}-M_t;x,y).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A decisive comparison shows that the P4 numerical formula and the crown specialization n(n-1)(n-2) are COVERED, despite different invariant names. They are not counted as originality. The independent content surviving this coverage is the simultaneously graded forest enumeration for every allowed triple, including disconnected forests and exceptional P5 cases. That entire statement is neither a corollary of just a P4 count nor evidently a known parameter substitution.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for the FULL three-parameter order-by-component induced-forest enumerator, not for its individual P4 consequence. Two earlier published exact results for precisely K_{p,q} minus a matching already imply the P4 coefficient t((p-1)(q-1)-t+1): respectively the number of disjoint maximal-clique/maximal-stable-set pairs and the number of length-three geodesics between missing matched pairs. They do not determine the entire forest polynomial, the P5 enumeration or the component-stratified all-size counts. The 2022 acyclic polynomial covers the univariate INVARIANT in general, but did not provide this family's matching deletion formula; the 2011 Q(G;x,y) counts ALL induced subgraphs, including cycles, rather than their forest-only subset, and treats K_{p,q} without deletions in Corollary 19. Related graph-wide extremal/induced-arboricity papers do not imply the family-specific coefficient theorem. Search failure is not novelty proof; older obscure tables/derivations remain possible.
residual_risks: Specific P4 enumeration and crown P4 count are ALREADY COVERED by two published same-family results; do not advertise those as independent discoveries.

evidence: Barton et al. 2022 introduced the acyclic polynomial because it encodes decycling/feedback-vertex-set order, a concrete mathematical motivation for specializing it.
The closed Phi(x,y) records component counts even for disconnected 2K2 configurations and isolate-plus-star cases, information missing from y=1 specialization.
Full three-parameter classification p,q,t and the crown boundary t=n distinguish the perturbation of complete-bipartite graphs with a missing matching.
value.rationale: The complete vertex-induced forest polynomial is a natural refinement of the acyclic polynomial and feedback-vertex-set number: for one basic three-parameter graph family it gives every order-by-component stratum and minimum feedback-set solution multiplicity, rather than an arbitrary finite slice. Matching deletion changes the unperturbed biclique star-only structure by exactly P4, 2K2 and P5 exceptions, a motivated finite structural classification. Although the P4 number by itself is known, neither that number nor a generic graph-polynomial definition determines the full bivariate component-resolved distribution; counting all disjoint forests is independently useful. The balanced P4-versus-P5 equality criterion and crown maximum-forest counts are exact consequences of that enumeration and not offered as independent unrelated achievements. No general arbitrary-deletion complexity result or a substantially more general graph family is claimed.
residual_risks: The derivation uses elementary combinatorial case counting and is not claimed to be a general graph-theoretic breakthrough.
Novel value would be diminished if a prior whole-polynomial formula is found; P4 subclaim already has a prior mathematical explanation.
